ideas: Better job prospects with an international degree
Cheaper alternatives like online or local programmes

phrases.meaning: widen someone's experience of the world

phrases.phrase: step out of their comfort zone
stand on their own two feet

phrases.meaning: be worth all the money spent

model: I think studying abroad is worth the cost, as long as students choose their course carefully. First, it can really help your career. An international degree helps graduates stand out to employers, and you build an international network. For example, my cousin used to work as a receptionist in Da Nang, but after doing a master's in Australia, she got a job at a multinational company and doubled her salary. So in her case, the degree has already paid for itself. Another reason is personal growth. Living in another country forces you to step out of your comfort zone and stand on your own two feet. My friend who studied in Korea would call her mum every day for help at first, but after a year she no longer needed anyone to sort things out for her. Of course, it can be a huge financial burden for families. But if the programme is good, I'd say it's worth every penny.
